newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India down after Bombay fall.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India down after Bombay fall.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished lower on Monday following local market losses in Bombay driven by concern over a possible hike in government-set oil prices, traders said.
They said there were few positive factors driving the market in the short term following the approval on Friday of the 1997/98 budget.
The pullback followed a run higher by GDR prices and premiums on Friday following the approval of the budget and in expectation of gains in India on Monday.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.55 points down at 78.37, with the premium over the local market at 20.91 percent from 22.32 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index shed 34.09 points to 3,735.25.
Reliance lost 21 cents to $18.50/19.50 and SBI slipped 17 cents to $23.50/24.50.

Another decline in Taipei stocks pulled Taiwanese GDRs lower amid continued political uncertainty. The Capel Taiwan GDR Index was down 2.75 points, or 2.24 percent, to 119.84, representing a discount to the local market of 3.95 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index added 0.23 points to 62.35 points, a premium of 35.68 percent over the local market.
